- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.
- Avoid over-optimism after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.0 to -1.0 in 3–5 days), lag forecast by 1–2 days to avoid premature reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a 2–3% downward bias to prevent over-leverage.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (±0.35+), apply a 1–2% smoothing filter to reduce forecast noise.
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.2) and forecast diverges >3% from true, revert to 14-day moving average for stability.
